clue.text: On-going panic

parts.note: read 'On-going' as 'going on', i.e. stepping out in front of an audience, and the panic is the nerves a performer feels then

explanation.surface: A description of ongoing, continuous panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-going' looks like 'continuing', but split it as 'going on': the moment an actor walks out in front of the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous dread felt by a performer about to appear before an audience is exactly this theatrical condition.

clue.text: A plug for the trainee — in the main a hard worker

indicators.note: 'in' puts the learner letter inside the run of the other two pieces

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
the ant is proverbially industrious
L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: A stopper offered to an apprentice working hard at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A plug' is the definition, not the start of the wordplay. Learner drivers in Britain display L-plates, hence trainee for the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used to fill and close gaps works as a stopper against leaks.

clue.text: Sharp helper receiving little credit

indicators.note: the helper word is receiving, i.e. taking in, the short form

parts.note: an aid is an assistant or helper
CR is the short form of credit in accounts

explanation.surface: An assistant who gets hardly any recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' could suggest clever, but here it describes a pungent smell or taste; 'receiving' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent, bitter smell or taste is described as sharp.

clue.text: Furnishing simple church music

parts.note: something easy is simple
an air is a tune or piece of music

explanation.surface: Plain furnishings and music in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furnishing' is a noun: one item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable upholstered armchair is one piece of furniture in a room.

clue.text: Back about car failing to start

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: the word car fails to start, i.e. loses its first letter, like an engine that will not turn over

explanation.surface: A driver goes back because the car won't start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' removes the first letter of 'car', leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: The hind part of anything is its back end.

clue.text: Six-footer, an environmentalist and shrewd with it

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party
fly is British slang for knowing or shrewd

explanation.surface: A tall person who is both an eco-campaigner and street-smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six legs. 'Fly' meaning shrewd is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are insects, and every insect has six legs.

clue.text: Object over the charge

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: 'it' is a pronoun for an object or thing

explanation.surface: Someone protests against the fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like the verb 'protest'; it is the noun, giving IT, which 'over' turns to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce once paid to the church was a levy, a compulsory charge.

clue.text: Still to be seen in up-to-date clothing for a youngster

indicators.note: the word for still is to be seen in, i.e. inside, the word for recent

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in 'the latest news'
yet means still, as in 'not yet'

explanation.surface: A child still dressed in fashionable clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adjective for calm, but it is the adverb meaning 'even now'; 'to be seen in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete set of garments prepared for a newborn baby is a layette.

clue.text: Identity of mutinous sea men confined in ship

indicators.note: the rebellious sailors are confined in the vessel letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: mutinous sailors are in revolt, so the letters of 'sea men' break out of order

explanation.surface: Rebellious sailors are locked up aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutinous' gives the rearrangement AMENES, and 'confined in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact likeness or being identical is the sense of identity meant here.

clue.text: It's high-rise accommodation for high-fliers!

parts.note: the 'accommodation' is room up in the sky, and the 'high-fliers' are aircraft and spacecraft, not ambitious executives

explanation.surface: A tower block of flats marketed to ambitious young executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-rise accommodation' suggests a tower block and 'high-fliers' successful people; read literally, it is the room above the Earth that flying machines use.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere and the region beyond it, where aircraft and rockets travel, together form this zone.

clue.text: Bad day to appear a flatterer

indicators.note: a bad version of the words 'day to' is a spoiled one, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad day for someone to turn out to be a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges DAYTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who fawns and flatters to win favour is called this.

clue.text: Make off with a book and pipe

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or channel carrying air or liquid

explanation.surface: Someone steals a book and a smoking pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to carry them off illegally, a stronger sense of taking away.

clue.text: Money received from the principal source

definitions.text: Money received from the principal source

parts.words: Money received from the principal source
parts.note: 'principal' here is the capital sum lent or invested, and the money it earns is the return on it

explanation.surface: Cash obtained from the head teacher or chief person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' suggests a person in charge; in finance it is the capital sum on which a borrower pays a percentage.
explanation.definitionFit: The return paid on a loan or deposit, calculated as a percentage of the capital, carries this name.

clue.text: Warning that is round about

indicators.note: the word 'that' is round, i.e. surrounds, the short word for about

parts.note: taken as written
RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A warning that something lies all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round about' reads as a phrase meaning roughly, but 'is round' is the container signal and 'about' its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A menacing statement of harm to come serves as a warning.

clue.text: Restricted allowance to a pound — so sensible

parts.note: a ration is a fixed, limited allowance
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Limiting spending to a pound is wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reasonable and logical in thought is the meaning of sensible.

clue.text: Be without a valet as a result of violence

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside': the letters of 'Be' sit outside the servant

parts.note: taken as written
a lackey is a manservant or footman, like a valet

explanation.surface: Someone told to manage without a personal servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be without a valet' reads as doing without help, but 'without' means outside: B and E wrap LACKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise around the eye from a punch is a typical injury from a fight.

clue.text: Woodman finding bird trapped in a carrier

indicators.note: the bird is trapped in, held inside, the carrier word

parts.note: a carter carries goods by cart
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A forester discovers a bird caught inside a transport container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woodman' suggests a forester, but here it is someone who works with wood; 'trapped in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who works with timber is a man of wood in that sense.

clue.text: A dreamer can be really sweet!

indicators.note: 'can be' says the letters of 'A dreamer' can be turned into another word

explanation.surface: A dreamy person may be truly lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges ADREAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A light brown cane sugar is something sweet.

clue.text: Held up trade possibly when in the red

indicators.note: 'in' places the rearranged letters inside the colour word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the word trade may appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Business was delayed during a period of being in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' gives the rearrangement TARDE, and 'in' is the container signal; 'in the red' looks like an idiom for debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slowed down or delayed has been held back.

clue.text: The city calls for some study

explanation.surface: A city demands that people do some studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls for' is a link. READING is a large town in Berkshire, west of London, often loosely called a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a large Berkshire town; perusing books is a kind of study.

clue.text: Forces others to go in different directions

indicators.note: 'to go in' says the word for others is put inside the two compass letters

parts.note: W and S are the compass points west and south, two different directions
the rest means the others, the remainder

explanation.surface: Other people are made to scatter in different directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' is a verb here, as in forcing something from someone's grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulls or extracts something with violent effort, as in seizing control.

clue.text: Getting wed, soon perhaps lost all sense of reality

indicators.note: 'perhaps' suggests the words 'wed soon' might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone about to marry was in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges WEDSOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Fainting or being overcome by rapture means losing consciousness of the world around.

clue.text: Note to the fellow keen to economise: spray

parts.note: A is a musical note
a miser hoards money and hates spending it

explanation.surface: A written message to a thrifty man about a spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that turns perfume or liquid into a fine mist is this kind of spray.

clue.text: A model's single business transaction

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A fashion model's one commercial agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example to be copied is a model, in the sense of a paragon.

clue.text: Wool may get in more of a tangle

indicators.note: being 'more of a tangle' means the letters of 'in more' are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Wool can become even more tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a tangle' rearranges INMORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine soft wool comes from this breed of sheep, so the fibre shares its name.

clue.text: Train that is about to speed up

indicators.note: 'about' says the abbreviation goes around the other piece

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to run is to speed

explanation.surface: A railway train is about to accelerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives the reversal NUR, and 'about' is the container signal; 'Train' is a verb here, toughen.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom someone to hardship by exposure is to toughen or train them.

clue.text: Firm request to stop talking in the club

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation of company, a firm
sh is the sound asking for quiet

explanation.surface: A company asks for silence in the members' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a weapon, not a society: a cosh is a short heavy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A short heavy bludgeon used as a weapon is a type of club.

clue.text: A little souvenir — a teeny cross

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at receiving only a tiny keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: Being angry or annoyed is the adjective sense of cross.

clue.text: An order resulting in revolution

parts.note: the order is a military drill command, and the revolution is the soldiers spinning round to face the opposite way, not a political uprising

explanation.surface: A decree that triggers a popular uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests overthrowing a government; on the parade ground it is a turn of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill command telling soldiers to wheel round and face the rear produces a half-turn.

clue.text: The earl made chief in southern England

indicators.note: 'made' says the words 'The earl' are made into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: A nobleman promoted to leader somewhere in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges THEEARL into LEATHER. LEATHERHEAD is a town in Surrey, a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey commuter town is a place located in the south of the country.
